title: FHE equality matching
description: Fully homomorphic encryption evaluates circuits on ciphertexts: to search, the server homomorphically compares the encrypted query against each encrypted document and returns encrypted match bits. The server learns nothing — not the query, not the documents, not even which matched (with the right protocol).
method: Encrypt query and corpus; homomorphic equality circuit per document; aggregate match bits; client decrypts the result.
usage: Use for the most sensitive searches; batch and preprocess to manage FHE cost.

demo.code:
print('query enc("urgent") vs 10k encrypted docs (FHE)')
print('server returns encrypted match vector; client decrypts: docs 3,7')

title: Wildcard and fuzzy encrypted search
description: Exact tokens aren't enough: wildcard and fuzzy search over encrypted data uses n-gram tokenization (encrypted n-grams match approximately) or homomorphic edit-distance circuits. 'Jon' finds 'John' without decrypting the directory — approximate matching under encryption.
method: Index encrypted n-grams; query expands to n-grams; rank by overlap; or compute homomorphic edit distance for precision.
usage: Use n-grams for interactive fuzzy search; reserve homomorphic edit distance for verification.

demo.code:
print('query "jon": n-grams {jo,on} match enc("john") n-grams {jo,oh,hn}')
print('ranked: John (0.67 overlap) -> returned')

title: Verifiable encrypted search
description: A malicious server could return wrong results; verifiable SSE adds proofs — the client checks completeness and correctness of results cryptographically. The server proves it searched the whole index honestly, or the client detects the lie.
method: Index with authentication (Merkle/hashes); server returns results + proof; client verifies before trusting.
usage: Use when the server isn't trusted for correctness; verification is cheap relative to search.

demo.code:
print('server returns 3 docs + Merkle proof of completeness')
print('client verifies: all matches returned, none omitted -> TRUSTED')

title: Forward-private dynamic indexes
description: When documents are added, the server shouldn't learn they match old queries (forward privacy). Dynamic SSE schemes re-key or re-randomize on update so new documents are unlinkable to past searches — the index evolves without leaking its own history.
method: Re-randomize index entries on update; queries use fresh trapdoors; the server can't link new docs to old queries.
usage: Require forward privacy for frequently-updated encrypted collections.

demo.code:
print('doc added: index entries re-randomized')
print('server cannot tell it matches last week\'s query: FORWARD PRIVATE')

title: Encrypted regex matching
description: Regular expressions over encrypted text via homomorphic automata evaluation: the regex compiles to an automaton, the server evaluates it homomorphically over encrypted characters. Log analysis and DLP on encrypted data — patterns matched, content unseen.
method: Compile regex to automaton; evaluate homomorphically per character; aggregate acceptance; client decrypts the verdict.
usage: Use for pattern scanning on encrypted logs; keep regexes small (automata cost).

demo.code:
print('regex: credit-card pattern over encrypted logs (FHE automaton)')
print('server: match at line 8812 (content unseen) -> alert with proof')

title: Performance engineering for encrypted search
description: Encrypted search is 10-1000x slower than plaintext; engineering closes the gap: index sharding, GPU/FPGA acceleration of homomorphic ops, hybrid plaintext-metadata indexes, and caching frequent queries. Performance is what separates research prototypes from deployed systems.
method: Shard indexes; accelerate crypto ops; hybridize where leakage allows; cache; measure relentlessly.
usage: Benchmark on your data; hybridize deliberately (document each leakage); cache aggressively.

demo.code:
print('baseline FHE search: 40s/query -> sharded + GPU: 1.2s')
print('hybrid metadata index: 80ms (leakage documented, accepted)')

title: Multi-keyword ranked encrypted search
description: Real search ranks: multi-keyword encrypted search computes relevance (TF-IDF style) over encrypted term frequencies using homomorphic addition or secure two-party ranking. Results come back ranked without the server seeing terms, frequencies, or the ranking computation's inputs.
method: Encrypt term frequencies; homomorphically accumulate scores; return top-k encrypted; client decrypts and verifies.
usage: Use for document search at scale; the homomorphic scoring is the cost center — optimize it.

demo.code:
print('query 3 keywords over 100k encrypted docs')
print('homomorphic scoring -> top-10 returned, ranked (server saw nothing)')

title: Order-revealing search indexes
description: Range queries on encrypted text (dates, versions) use order-revealing or order-preserving encryption in the index: the server compares ciphertexts to answer ranges without decrypting. The leakage (order) is modeled and accepted for the columns that need it.
method: Index with ORE/OPE; range queries compare ciphertext; document order leakage per column.
usage: Use only for range-needed columns; model what order reveals about your data.

demo.code:
print('range [2026-01-01, 2026-06-01] on encrypted dates')
print('server compares ciphertext order -> returns matches (order leaked, accepted)')
